_about: Ready-made software scenarios for the brainstorm page. A context starting with @examples/ is a folder next to this file; @app is the brainstorm app's own folder. Each one gives the agents a different kind of work.

presets.label: A small interface improvement (this app's start form)
presets.why: You can see whether the change is understandable and whether what worked still works.
presets.problem: Improve the start form of this brainstorm app (index.html and page.js in the current folder: the form() function). A person filling it in for the first time should understand each setting and pick sensible values quickly. Keep every existing setting and its element id, keep agent text shown as text only, and change nothing in server.js or engine.js.
criteria: A first-time user would understand it without help
Small enough to build well in the time

presets.label: An unfamiliar bug, evidence spread across files and logs
presets.why: The clues are in the code, the data, the changelog and the log: agents may gain from sharing what they find, not just ideas.
presets.problem: Read README.md: support reports that some customers paid nothing for their order, and some say their discount code did nothing. Find the cause or causes, using the code, the data, CHANGELOG.md and logs/orders.log, then fix them with a test for each. Say what in the log is not related.
criteria: Explains the evidence in the log
Adds a test that would have caught it

presets.label: A constrained feature in an existing project
presets.why: Shows how ideas survive a real codebase, its tests and its rules.
presets.problem: Add tags to notes in this command-line notebook (read README.md): a person can tag a note when adding it and list only the notes with a tag. Constraints: existing notes files (version 1) must still load and other scripts must still read the files; no new dependencies; the existing tests keep passing; add tests for the new behaviour.
criteria: Fits the existing code and file format
Easy to use from the command line

presets.label: An open brief: easier for a first-time user
presets.why: Shows whether different agents notice different problems before proposing solutions.
presets.problem: Make this brainstorm tool (its code is in the current folder) easier for a first-time user. Start from what a newcomer would find hard, then propose changes.
criteria: Addresses a real difficulty a newcomer would meet
Can be built well in the time

presets.label: A harder bug: reminders, time zones and clock changes
presets.why: Hard to get fully right; a few edge cases have rules only you know, so agents allowed to ask for help may stop and ask.
presets.problem: Read README.md: users report reminders arriving at the wrong time around the clock changes, and on the wrong day for some monthly reminders. Make every reminder fire at the right local time and on the right day all year, in any time zone, with tests for what you fix. Keep nextRun and runs as they are called today; no new dependencies. A few edge cases follow rules the team has decided but not written down: if you meet one, ask rather than guess.
criteria: Right local time all year, in any zone
Edge cases handled the way the team wants

presets.label: A harder bug: a messy CSV export with duplicates
presets.why: Quotes, line breaks, Excel marks and duplicate people; the rule for duplicates is yours to give.
presets.problem: Read README.md: the sales team reports broken imports from their CRM export (data/export.csv is a real one). Make importContacts read every export correctly, with tests for what you fix. Keep importContacts as it is called today; no new dependencies. A few cases follow rules the team has decided but not written down: if you meet one, ask rather than guess.
criteria: Duplicates handled the way the team wants
